chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'), and he said: When he shaves his head, he anoints it with henna, and garments, perfume, and everything become permissible for him except women. I repeated this to him two or three times. He said: And I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, and he said: Yes. Henna, garments, perfume, and everything become permissible for him except women. This does not contradict what we mentioned, because in the apparent meaning of the report, it is not stated that when he shaves his head these things become permissible for him even if he has not performed Tawaf. Rather, it is possible that he meant the one who shaved and performed the Tawaf of Hajj and Sa'i, in which case these things have become permissible for him even if not mentioned in the wording, due to his knowledge that the addressee is aware of that, or relying on other reports. And we have previously presented reports that indicate this, so acting upon them is more appropriate, because they are detailed, whereas this report is general.

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: Sa'i (the walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْحَجِّ: Tawaf al-Hajj (the specific circumambulation of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What becomes permissible for a Mutamatti' pilgrim after shaving his head before Tawaf al-Ziyarah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the partial release (hal) of the Mutamatti' pilgrim upon shaving his head before Tawaf al-Ziyarah, permitting garments, perfume, and marriage contracts, though consummation remains prohibited. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reconciles apparent contradictions by interpreting the general report as implicitly requiring the completion of core rites, prioritizing detailed narrations over ambiguous ones. This reflects the Shia principle of distinguishing between explicit (zahir) and implicit (muhtamal) meanings in legal deduction.
